U.A. Sports Festival.text: The U.A. Sports Festival is the biggest sporting event in Japan. Once Quirks made fair international competition impossible, the Olympics shrank to a shadow of their old scale, and U.A.'s yearly festival took their place in public interest: every spring, crowds of tens of thousands and a national television audience watch the academy's students compete. Each year group has its own events, all four courses compete together within a year, and the first-year events in U.A. Stadium draw the biggest crowds because the faces are new. The preliminary events change every year and stay secret until the day, chosen by the chief referee; past festivals have opened with races, team battles and obstacle courses before narrowing the field to one-on-one bouts on a concrete stage that Cementoss raises in the arena. Midnight has refereed the first-year events in recent years, and Present Mic calls them from the broadcast booth. Pro heroes fill reserved sections to scout, and the offers agencies send afterward decide where first-years spend their first workplace experience. For General Studies, Support and Management students it is the one stage the whole country watches: a strong General Studies showing can earn a Hero Course transfer, Support students show off their gear to the support companies, and Management students track who draws the cameras. Every bout is supervised and nonlethal; the referee stops a fight that turns dangerous, and Recovery Girl works from a treatment room under the stands. Students of other academies never compete, but many watch the broadcast.
